# Upgrade OpenAI realtime to gpt-realtime-2.1 + centralize model config

## Context

The OpenAI engine currently targets `gpt-realtime-2`. OpenAI has released **gpt-realtime-2.1** (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/models/gpt-realtime-2.1) — a drop-in successor on the same `v1/realtime` endpoint at identical pricing, with improved alphanumeric recognition, silence/noise handling, and interruption behavior. No `session.update` or `client_secrets` API changes are involved, so this is a pure model-string bump.

The problem is the string lives in **three independently-maintained places** with nothing enforcing agreement:

1. `lib/realtime/openai-agent.ts:198` — `BASE.model`, sent client-side in `session.update`
2. `app/api/openai/token/route.ts:18` — `const MODEL`, used server-side to mint the ephemeral client secret
3. `lib/data.ts:124` — the display string in the Providers UI

If (1) and (2) ever disagree, the mint scope and the session config diverge silently. xAI and Gemini don't have this problem (model lives only in their agent module); OpenAI is the sole exception because its mint route also needs the model.

**Decisions made with the user:** scope is OpenAI only (xAI/Gemini already have a single source of truth — no churn there), and the form is a JSON file under `config/`, mirroring the existing `config/lm-models.json` → `lib/realtime/lm-config.ts` pattern.

## Changes

### 1. New: `config/realtime-models.json`

Keyed by engine so it can grow later, but populated only for openai per the agreed scope:

```json
{
  "openai": {
    "model": "gpt-realtime-2.1",
    "transcriptionModel": "gpt-realtime-whisper"
  }
}
```

`transcriptionModel` is included because it's the other model string in `BASE` (`openai-agent.ts:201`) — one file to touch for any future model bump.

### 2. New: `lib/realtime/realtime-model-config.ts`

Small client-safe module mirroring `lib/realtime/lm-config.ts` (header comment style included — see that file's lines 1–8). No secrets, JSON import only:

```ts
import catalog from "@/config/realtime-models.json";

export const OPENAI_REALTIME_MODEL: string = catalog.openai.model;
export const OPENAI_TRANSCRIPTION_MODEL: string = catalog.openai.transcriptionModel;
```

(A typed `RealtimeModelCatalog` interface + `as unknown as` cast like `lm-config.ts:36-42` if the inferred JSON type isn't sufficient.)

### 3. Consume it in the three duplication sites

- **`lib/realtime/openai-agent.ts`** — `BASE` (lines 194–205): `model: OPENAI_REALTIME_MODEL`, `transcription: { model: OPENAI_TRANSCRIPTION_MODEL, ... }`. This module is deliberately client-safe (its only current import is `@/lib/firecrawl/config`); a JSON-backed config module keeps that property.

- **`lib/data.ts`** — `PROVIDERS[id="openai"].model` (line 124): use `OPENAI_REALTIME_MODEL` instead of the literal.

### 4. Sweep stale version references

Update `gpt-realtime-2` → `gpt-realtime-2.1` (or version-neutral wording where the version doesn't matter) in:

- Comments: `lib/realtime/openai-agent.ts` (lines 2, 10, 38, 63, 90, 94), `lib/realtime/use-openai-session.ts:3`, `lib/realtime/use-realtime-session.ts:44`
- Docs: `README.md` (lines ~93, 106, 421–422 — also document the new config file alongside the existing lm-models/voice-models mentions), `docs/persona-architecture.md` (lines ~5, 72, 79, 237–245, 269)
- `CLAUDE.md` architecture map if it names the model version

## Reused patterns

- `config/lm-models.json` + `lib/realtime/lm-config.ts` — the exact "model config as data" pattern being mirrored
- `providerModelLabel()` in `lm-config.ts:76-83` needs no change — it passes through `provider.model` for non-cascade engines, which now resolves from the config file via `lib/data.ts`

1. Gates in order: `bunx tsc --noEmit` → `bun run lint` → `bun run fmt:check` (run `bun run fmt` first if new files) → `bun run build`
2. `rg -n "gpt-realtime-2\b"` returns no hits outside git history (i.e. no stale `gpt-realtime-2` without the `.1`)

   - `POST /api/openai/token` succeeds (mint accepts `gpt-realtime-2.1`)
   - WebRTC session connects, agent greets, transcription appears
   - Providers panel shows `gpt-realtime-2.1` as the model label

Done. The OpenAI engine now runs **gpt-realtime-2.1**, and the model id lives in one place.

## What changed

**New centralized config** (mirroring the existing `lm-models.json` pattern):
- [config/realtime-models.json](config/realtime-models.json) — `{ "openai": { "model": "gpt-realtime-2.1", "transcriptionModel": "gpt-realtime-whisper" } }`. Future model bumps are a one-line edit here.
- [lib/realtime/realtime-model-config.ts](lib/realtime/realtime-model-config.ts) — client-safe module exporting `OPENAI_REALTIME_MODEL` / `OPENAI_TRANSCRIPTION_MODEL`.

**The three former duplication sites now all import from it:**
- [openai-agent.ts:200](lib/realtime/openai-agent.ts:200) — `BASE.model` (sent in `session.update`)
- [route.ts:44](app/api/openai/token/route.ts:44) — the ephemeral-token mint body (deleted the local `MODEL` constant, so mint scope and session config can no longer silently disagree)
- [data.ts:126](lib/data.ts:126) — the Providers UI label

Also swept stale `gpt-realtime-2` mentions in comments, README (including documenting the new config file in the architecture map), and hook doc comments — `rg "gpt-realtime-2(?!\.1)"` now returns nothing.

## Verification

- All four gates pass: `bunx tsc --noEmit`, `bun run lint`, `bun run fmt:check`, `bun run build`.
- **Live mint verified**: `POST /api/openai/token` against the running dev server returned 200 with an ephemeral key whose session is scoped to `"model": "gpt-realtime-2.1"` — OpenAI accepts the new id.
- The Providers panel renders **OPENAI · gpt-realtime-2.1** (screenshot above), and the call header shows **VIA OPENAI · GPT-REALTIME-2.1**.
- One caveat: I couldn't complete a full audio call because microphone capture is blocked in the in-app browser — the session correctly reported "microphone permission denied" and ended cleanly. The WebRTC path itself is unchanged by this refactor, but if you want to hear 2.1's improved interruption/noise handling, the dev server is still running on `localhost:3000` for you to place a real call.

Memory updated to reflect the 2.1 bump and the new config file.

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
- The bug class this kills is *silent divergence*: the mint route scopes the ephemeral key to a model server-side while the client's `session.update` names it independently — nothing type-checks that agreement, so a half-done bump would fail only at call time.
- Putting the id in JSON (not a TS constant in the agent module) matters for import direction: the server route can import a data-only module without pulling the whole client agent graph (prompts, Firecrawl config) into the API bundle.
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`
